source: NewtonBench (2025) benchmarking scientific law discovery in LLM agents
finding: Agents must design experiments and recover counterfactually shifted physical laws. Strong reasoning models do far better than non-reasoning ones.
numbers: 324 tasks from 108 shifted laws in 12 domains; 11 LLMs, 4 runs each. Symbolic accuracy (no code): GPT-5 75.9, Gemini-2.5-pro 65.4, o4-mini 47.8, DeepSeek-R1 43.4, GPT-4.1 5.8, GPT-4.1-mini 5.1. Non-thinking models under 10% overall.
limits: Read in two slices (to char 100000, then a later slice); canonical-vs-shifted drop not extracted. Physics only.
agent_relevance: Model-based hypothesis building from data is weak in non-reasoning models; reasoning budget matters more than prompts for O6.

source: NewtonBench (2025) benchmarking scientific law discovery in LLM agents
finding: Difficulty grows sharply when the system is complex (many interacting parts), not when the equation itself is harder.
numbers: GPT-5 vanilla: 90.3 easy, 90.3 medium, 87.5 hard. GPT-5 complex system: 72.9, 63.2, 40.3. Gemini-2.5-pro vanilla hard 69.4, complex hard 16.7. Domain range 18% to 54%; Bose-Einstein lowest at 18.1%.
limits: Single benchmark, simulated systems.
agent_relevance: Isolating sub-models, as Maxwell did with partial models, should be tested as a scaffold step; system complexity is the killer.

source: NewtonBench (2025) benchmarking scientific law discovery in LLM agents
finding: A code interpreter helps weak models and slightly hurts strong ones, because strong models explore less when they can compute.
numbers: Symbolic accuracy change with code: GPT-4.1 +13.1, GPT-4.1-mini +9.6, DeepSeek-V3 +4.4; Gemini-2.5-flash -9.7, DeepSeek-R1 -6.0, GPT-5-mini -5.0, GPT-5 -2.6. Experiments run: Gemini-flash 23.41 vanilla vs 14.36 with code; GPT-4.1 80.59 vs 30.90.
limits: Tool effect confounded with experiment count; one benchmark.
agent_relevance: Do not let code replace probing experiments; keep exploration when a check fails (G1).

source: NewtonBench (2025) benchmarking scientific law discovery in LLM agents
finding: Small observation noise already damages law discovery. One model collected a large dataset, then submitted a wrong inverse-square law without fitting the exponent.
numbers: GPT-5-mini at noise 0.0001 lost 12-16% relative accuracy. Judge agreement with humans: GPT-4.1 98.3%; judge accuracy 0-shot 93.33, 7-shot 98.33.
limits: Noise tested on one model.
agent_relevance: Fit exponents numerically in code; test on what the answer was not fitted to (G3).

source: Hla (2025) Machina Mirabilis: an LLM trained only on pre-1900 text
finding: Small-scale test of the Hassabis idea: can a model with no post-1900 knowledge reach Planck or Einstein-style steps? Result: only glimpses.
numbers: 3.3B parameters, about 22B pre-1900 tokens, 290M physics midtraining tokens, 30M instruction tokens. CORE: pre-1900 0.1400, pre-1905 0.1632, pre-1964 0.1897, FineWeb-Edu 0.2602. Outputs: light made up of definite quantities of energy; sometimes sees equipartition fails at high frequency; for the elevator usually proposes an ether-like pull, rarely local equivalence of gravity and acceleration.
limits: Blog, not peer reviewed. Four topics, scored by feel with an LLM judge; author warns of parroting, reward hacking and leakage.
agent_relevance: Concept change at an impasse is rare even with the evidence in the prompt; do not expect a model to reframe without scaffolding.

source: Hla (2025) Machina Mirabilis: filtering and contamination
finding: Documents with any flagged post-1900 term were dropped whole; also year-label, OCR and token log-prior filters.
numbers: Data from Institutional Books, British Library books, American Stories newspapers. Midtraining was 1.32% of pretraining corpus.
limits: Filtering may remove useful info and may still leak; the judge model has modern knowledge.
agent_relevance: A clean-cutoff replay is the right design for testing cognitive-historical claims on LLMs; build agent test sets this way.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) matched or beat college students on text matrices, letter-string and verbal analogies but was weaker on far story analogies.
numbers: Digit matrices: 40 humans; generative OR=1.88, multiple choice OR=6.27. Letter strings: 57 humans, OR=1.76, subtype r=0.7. Story analogies: 54 humans; GPT-3 near p=0.0039, far p=0.065 (not significant); humans better, OR=0.37.
limits: First 100000 characters read. GPT-4 described as stronger without numbers. No long-term memory; weak physical reasoning (gumball task).
agent_relevance: Surface analogy is available; the weak part is far, causal, physical transfer, the Maxwell-type analogy (O7).

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Counterfactual tasks for analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Failed generalisation: letter-string analogies in permuted or symbol alphabets break the models but not humans.
numbers: Accuracy over all alphabets: humans 0.753 (136 recruited), GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452. Alphabets with 2, 5, 10, 20 letters permuted plus 40 symbol problems.
limits: Zero-generalisation only; chain of thought not tested; participant pools differ from Webb.
agent_relevance: Analogy success may be pattern memory; require a mutated mapping as the check (G3).

source: Stevenson et al. (2024) Can LLMs generalize analogy solving like children can?
finding: Adults and 7-9 year olds keep performance across new alphabets; every LLM drops, most on symbols.
limits: Table counts differ slightly from the methods text (54 vs 55 runs; 41 vs 42 children).
agent_relevance: Boundary for O7: LLM analogy collapses as surface features move away from training; test mappings on abstracted symbols.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners
finding: Analogical prompting: the model writes its own related problems, then solves the target. Beats 0-shot and few-shot CoT by small margins.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5-turbo: 0-shot CoT 75.8, 5-shot CoT 76.7, self-generated exemplars 77.8. MATH: 33.9, 34.9, 37.3. text-davinci-003 GSM8K: 50.3, 54.0, 61.0. Codeforces GPT-4 Acc@1: 16 (0-shot), 17 (3-shot), 19 (knowledge+exemplars).
limits: Gains small on strong models. Needs a strong model: curie-001 stays 2%. More tokens. 12 of 50 failures were exemplar-to-target generalisation gaps.
agent_relevance: A subfield method already used in a prompt loop. Use as candidate generator, checked in code.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners
finding: Ablations: diverse exemplars beat non-diverse; about 3 exemplars is enough; self-consistency adds more than the analogy step.
numbers: K=1..5 GSM8K: 76.1, 77.0, 77.5, 77.3, 77.8. Diverse 77.8/37.3 vs non-diverse 75.9/35.2 (GSM8K/MATH). Plus self-consistency: 85.3 / 46.0.
limits: GPT-3.5-turbo only.
agent_relevance: Voting from one model is not independent (G4), so treat the self-consistency gain with caution; the diversity result supports forcing different analogy sources.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs generate novel research ideas?
finding: Blind expert review: LLM ideas rated more novel than expert human ideas, not more feasible.
numbers: 104 participants (49 writers, 79 reviewers), 298 reviews, 49 ideas per condition. Novelty 4.84 human vs 5.64 AI vs 5.81 AI+human rerank (review-level). Feasibility 6.61 vs 6.34. Only about 200 of 4000 seed ideas per topic non-duplicate (cosine 0.8). Best LLM judge agreed with humans 53.3% vs 56.1% human-human.
limits: NLP prompting topics only; ideas not executed; human ideas were median quality.
agent_relevance: Generating novel combinations is easy; selection and diversity are the bottleneck (G5).

source: SciMON (2023) scientific inspiration machines
finding: Retrieval of semantic, knowledge-graph and citation neighbours as inspiration, plus an iterative novelty check against literature.
numbers: Expert helpfulness: GPT-4 few-shot 73%, GPT-4+KG 66%, GPT-3.5 few-shot 33%. Novelty loop (cosine over 0.6): 55.6% of updated ideas gained novelty in iteration one, 57.8% in two. Ground-truth ideas better in 85% of pairs. Relation extraction precision 65.4%.
limits: Ideas often superficial recombinations; seed term from ground truth; NLP and PubMed only.
agent_relevance: Novelty checks by code against an index are the model for checking analogy output.

source: MOOSE (2023) LLMs for open-domain hypothesis discovery
finding: Pipeline of background, inspiration and hypothesis, with three feedback modules, raises novelty with unchanged validity. Inspiration is the analogy slot.
numbers: 50 papers after Jan 2023. GPT-4 judge novelty (1-5): baseline 2.483, MOOSE-base 3.081, +future feedback 3.226, +past feedback 3.390. Experts (3 PhD students, 400 hypotheses): novelty 2.276 to 3.197; validness about flat (3.579 to 3.750).
limits: Small, mostly marketing; no rediscovery rate; validness may be graded by familiarity.
agent_relevance: Separating background from inspiration is a usable structured form of the cognitive-historical pattern.

source: MOOSE-Chem (2024) rediscovering chemistry hypotheses
finding: Closest LLM test of historical rediscovery: given background, find the inspirations and rebuild the hypothesis.
numbers: 51 chemistry papers (2024). Inspiration hit ratio top 4%, corpus 300: GPT-4o 83.7%, Llama-70B 83.0%, Llama-8B 43.5%. Matched score top: MOOSE-Chem 4.020, MOOSE 2.882, SciMON 2.549. Experts on 51: score 4: 2, 3: 19, 2: 16, 1: 8, 0: 6, 5: 0.
limits: GPT-4o judge; cutoff stated as Oct or Dec 2023; none reached full score.
agent_relevance: Retrieving the right distant source is feasible; combining into a full theory is not yet.

source: LLM-SRBench (2025)
finding: On shifted or synthetic equation problems accuracy is low; Feynman-style benchmarks mostly measure memory.
numbers: 239 problems: 111 LSR-Transform, 128 LSR-Synth. Best symbolic accuracy 31.53% (LLM-SR, GPT-4o-mini) on Transform, 28.1% on Synth; best Acc0.1 50.45 (LaSR).
limits: Small models only (Llama-3.1-8B, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-3.5).
agent_relevance: Benchmarks built from famous historical laws leak; use transformed or counterfactual cases.

source: LLM-SR (2024) equation discovery via programming
finding: LLM prior knowledge plus program form, fitting in code and an evolutionary buffer beats symbolic regression baselines in most cases.
numbers: E. coli growth NMSE: LLM-SR Mixtral 0.0026/0.0037 vs PySR 0.0376/1.0141. About 2.5K iterations vs 2M+ for baselines. Exception: Oscillation 2 out-of-domain, Mixtral 0.0291 worse than uDSR 0.0015.
limits: Read to char 100000; ablation detail thin.
agent_relevance: A concrete loop: LLM proposes model form, code fits and scores, buffer keeps best. Fits the code-selects rule.

source: AI Feynman (2020)
finding: Older system with no LLM: dimensional analysis, symmetry and separability recover physics laws.
numbers: 100 Feynman equations: AI Feynman 100% vs Eureqa 71% (conclusion says 68%). 20 bonus: 90% vs 15%. Without dimensional analysis 93%. Most recovered at noise 1e-4; about half at 1e-2.
limits: Page inconsistent on Eureqa; Feynman equations are likely in LLM training data.
agent_relevance: Imposing structure (units, symmetry) is the machine form of model constraints in O6.

source: AI-Newton (2025) concept-driven physical law discovery
finding: Symbolic system with a concept base and plausible reasoning rediscovers Newton's second law, energy conservation and gravitation from raw data. No LLM used.
numbers: 46 classical mechanics experiments; about 90 concepts and 50 general laws on average; up to 1200 trials; average runtime 48 hours.
limits: Rediscovery only; proof of concept; authors suggest LLMs could replace the DSL later.
agent_relevance: Supports building concepts incrementally (Nersessian: gradual change) rather than in one step.

source: Li, Ji, Zhang (2022) From Kepler to Newton: explainable AI for science discovery
finding: Explainable AI rediscovers Kepler's laws and Newton's gravitation from Tycho Brahe data, framed as the cycle observation, hypothesis, prediction, experiment.
numbers: No figures on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only; workshop paper.
agent_relevance: Supports the cycle structure; no measured effect available.

source: ScienceAgentBench (2024)
finding: Agents solve about a third of real data-driven science tasks; execution feedback matters more than agent framework complexity.
numbers: 102 tasks from 44 papers. Claude-3.5-Sonnet self-debug 32.4% (34.3% with expert knowledge). o1-preview 42.2% at over 10x cost. Self-debug $0.057 vs OpenHands $0.958 per task; direct prompting worst.
limits: First 100000 chars read. GPT-4o judge for figures.
agent_relevance: Revising from real execution output (G2) beats heavier agent frameworks.

source: DiscoveryWorld (2024)
finding: A virtual lab with 120 discovery tasks shows a large gap between humans and agents.
numbers: 8 themes x 3 levels x 5 seeds. Human scientists (N=11) completion 66%, knowledge 55%. Best agent ReAct: 38% easy, 18% challenge. Hypothesizer found 34% of gold knowledge easy, 8% challenge. All GPT-4o.
limits: Only GPT-4o baselines; full run costs USD 3k-10k.
agent_relevance: Explicit hypothesis tracking helped knowledge but not completion; the hard part is the impasse stage.

source: SciAgents (2024)
finding: Knowledge-graph path sampling between distant concepts plus multi-agent critique generates cross-domain hypotheses.
numbers: Graph: 33,159 nodes, 48,753 edges from about 1000 papers. Five runs scored novelty/feasibility 8/7, 8/7, 6/8, 7/8, 8/7 by the system's own Assistant. No experimental validation.
limits: Self-scored; no human baseline; page does not describe a formal analogy mapping.
agent_relevance: Distant-concept linking is cheap; scoring is circular unless code or experiments check it.

source: Chain-of-Ideas agent (2024)
finding: Organising literature as a chain of ideas (anchor, forward and backward extension) gives ideas close to real papers.
numbers: Human ELO ideas: Real Paper 1100, CoI 1085, RAG 1029, AI-Scientist 812. Ablation without chain 42.4 vs full 50. Gains level off at chain length 5. GPT-4o agrees with humans 70.8% on ideas. Cost from $0.50 per idea.
limits: 50 topics; feasibility remains weak.
agent_relevance: An idea-lineage trace as context is a small cognitive-historical device that helps generation.

source: Officechai coverage of Machina Mirabilis (2025)
finding: Secondary report frames the Hassabis test as an LLM with data cut at 1911 discovering relativity.
numbers: No numbers beyond the Hla blog.
limits: Search snippet only.
agent_relevance: Benchmark framing only; cite no numbers.

source: LLM-Feynman (2025) arXiv 2503.06512
finding: Search snippet says LLM plus symbolic regression with domain knowledge rediscovers over 90% of Feynman-lecture formulas.
numbers: Over 90% (snippet).
limits: HTML page 404; not opened. Feynman data likely seen in training.
agent_relevance: Treat as unverified; likely memorisation (see LLM-SRBench).

source: Nersessian (2008) Creating Scientific Concepts
finding: Book blurbs: conceptual change comes from analogy, imagery and thought experiment (model-based reasoning) through many incremental models, shown in Maxwell and a think-aloud subject.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Blurb only; preface could not be read.
agent_relevance: Human side of O6 and O7 that the LLM studies try to copy.
